transcription.text:
Which of the following are the dimensions of communication?
Dimensions:
i) Downward
ii) Upward
iii) Horizontal/Lateral
iv) Diagonal
v) Grapevine
vi) Circular
options: i, ii, iii, iv and v
transcription.printedErrors: Option 3 repeats 'iv' ('i, iv and iv only').
transcription.changes: Option 1: 'i, i, iii' → 'i, ii, iii'; Option 2: 'ili' → 'iii'

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
In business communication, the **dimensions (directions) of communication** describe the paths along which messages flow in an organisation:
- **Downward**: from superiors to subordinates (orders, policies).
- **Upward**: from subordinates to superiors (reports, feedback, grievances).
- **Horizontal/Lateral**: between people at the same level.
- **Diagonal (cross-wise)**: between people at different levels in different departments.
- **Grapevine**: the informal network that flows in all directions.
'Circular' is not listed as a dimension; it is a pattern of a communication network (circle network), not a direction of flow. So i, ii, iii, iv and v are the dimensions, which is option A.
Why not the others: B, C and D each leave out recognised dimensions such as downward or diagonal.

transcription.text: Which of the following correctly defines coplanar force?
options: When the lines of the action of all forces lie in one plane.
Two or more than two forces acting at a point.
A single force, which acting along with other forces, keeps the body in equilibrium.
A single force which produces the same effect as that produced by two or more forces acting on the body.

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
Forces are **coplanar** when the lines of action of all the forces lie in **one plane**. That is exactly option A.
Why not the others:
- B (forces acting at a point) defines **concurrent** forces.
- C (a single force that, together with the other forces, keeps the body in equilibrium) defines the **equilibrant**.
- D (a single force producing the same effect as several forces together) defines the **resultant**.
Coplanar forces may or may not be concurrent; the only condition is that all their lines of action lie in the same plane.

transcription.text:
Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements?
i) Physical quantities which have magnitude only are called scalar quantities.
ii) Physical quantities which have both magnitude and direction are called vector quantities.
iii) Two equal and opposite parallel forces acting at different points in a body constitute a couple.
transcription.changes: il → ii; iil → iii; Iwo → Two; options: 1-True → i-True, Tre → True, il/ill → ii/iii

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
Check each statement:
- i) **True**. A scalar has magnitude only (mass, time, temperature).
- ii) **True**. A vector has magnitude and direction (force, velocity, displacement); strictly it must also follow vector addition, but this is the standard definition.
- iii) **True**. A **couple** is a pair of equal, opposite, parallel forces whose lines of action do not coincide (they act at different points). Its resultant force is zero but it produces a turning effect (moment = force × perpendicular distance).
All three are true, so the answer is option A (i-True, ii-True, iii-True).

transcription.text:
Which of the following protocols assign(s) dynamic IP?
i) POP
ii) DHCP
iii) BOOTP
iv) SNMP
v) ICMP
options: i, ii, iii and v only
ii, iii, iv and v only

subject: Computer Science
concept: Protocols that assign IP addresses (DHCP, BOOTP)
explanation:
IP addresses are handed out to hosts by **address-configuration protocols**:
- **DHCP** (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) leases IP addresses dynamically from a pool.
- **BOOTP** (Bootstrap Protocol) is the predecessor of DHCP; a BOOTP server supplies a booting host with its IP address. (Strictly, BOOTP uses a pre-configured table, and DHCP extended it with dynamic leasing, but BOOTP is the other protocol in the list that assigns IPs.)
The rest do not assign addresses:
- **POP** retrieves e-mail from a mail server.
- **SNMP** monitors and manages network devices.
- **ICMP** reports errors and diagnostics (ping, destination unreachable).
So the answer is ii and iii only, option B.

transcription.text: Which of the following security services protects against repudiation?

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
**Repudiation** means a sender or receiver later denies having sent or received a message. The security service that protects against this is **nonrepudiation**, usually provided by digital signatures: the message carries proof (signed with the sender's private key) that only the sender could have produced.
Why not the others:
- **Access control** prevents unauthorised use of resources.
- **Authentication** confirms the identity of a communicating party.
- **Data integrity** ensures the data was not modified in transit.
These are separate services in the ITU-T X.800 list; only nonrepudiation (option A) addresses denial of participation.

transcription.text:
Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements?
i) Service Set Identification (SSID) is human readable text string with a maximum length of 2000 bytes.
ii) Service Set Identification (SSID) acts as a single shared identifier between the access points and clients.

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
The **SSID** is the name of a Wi-Fi (IEEE 802.11) network.
- i) **False**. An SSID is a case-sensitive text string with a maximum length of **32 bytes** (octets), not 2000 bytes.
- ii) **True**. All access points and client devices of one wireless network use the same SSID, so it acts as a single shared identifier that a client uses to join that network.
So the correct combination is i-False, ii-True, which is option B.

transcription.text:
Which of the following languages are object-oriented programming languages?
Languages:
i) LISP
ii) Java
iii) C++
iv) Simula
v) SQL
vi) C
options: i, ii, iii and iv only
i, ii, iii, iv, v and vi

subject: Computer Science
keyNote: The key (A) counts LISP as object-oriented. Classic LISP is a functional/list-processing language; it is object-oriented only through the later CLOS extension of Common Lisp. Textbook classification gives ii, iii and iv (option B), so both A and B can be argued.
explanation:
Check each language:
- **Java** and **C++**: object-oriented (classes, inheritance, polymorphism).
- **Simula**: Simula 67 introduced classes and objects and is regarded as the first object-oriented language.
- **SQL**: a declarative database query language, not OOP.
- **C**: a procedural language, not OOP.
- **LISP**: originally a **functional**, list-processing language. Object orientation came later through extensions, chiefly **CLOS** (Common Lisp Object System), which is part of ANSI Common Lisp.
On the usual textbook classification, the OOP languages are Java, C++ and Simula, which is option B. The source key marks option A, which also includes LISP. That is defensible only if LISP is taken to mean Common Lisp with CLOS, so the question is ambiguous.

transcription.text: Which of the following is NOT a valid Software Life Cycle Model?

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
Recognised software development life cycle models and approaches include Waterfall, Iterative, Incremental, Prototype, Spiral, V-model, RAD and Agile.
- **JAD** (Joint Application Development) is a requirements and design approach in which users and developers work together in structured workshops. It is listed among SDLC methodologies.
- **Iterative** model: the product is built in repeated cycles, each refining the previous version.
- **Prototype** model: a working prototype is built and refined using customer feedback before the final system.
- **Circular** is not a named SDLC model. (The Spiral model is cyclic, but 'Circular model' is not a recognised name.)
So the answer is option D.

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
`&` applied to two `int` values is the **bitwise AND** operator: a result bit is 1 only if both input bits are 1.
- a = 5 = `0101`
- b = 7 = `0111`
- a & b = `0101` = 5
The brackets around `(a & b)` make the AND happen first, and then the result is concatenated to the string, so the program prints `a&b = 5` (option A).
Why not the others: 7 would be `a | b` (bitwise OR), 35 is `a * b`, and 2 is `a ^ b` (XOR: 0101 ^ 0111 = 0010).

transcription.text: ______ is a discipline which deals with the application of economic theory to business management.

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
**Business economics** (also called managerial economics) applies economic theory and tools of analysis to business decision-making, such as demand forecasting, pricing, production and cost decisions, and capital budgeting. The classic definition (Spencer and Siegelman) calls it the integration of economic theory with business practice to help management make decisions and plan ahead.
Why not the others:
- **MIS** provides information to managers for routine decisions.
- **Decision Support System** is an interactive computer system that helps with semi-structured decisions.
- **Information processing** is the conversion of data into information.
None of these is a discipline applying economic theory, so the answer is option A.

transcription.text: What is the full form of WPF with respect to ASP.NET?

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
**WPF** stands for **Windows Presentation Foundation**. It is Microsoft's UI framework in .NET for building Windows desktop applications. It uses **XAML** (an XML-based markup language) to describe the user interface and supports data binding, styles, templates, vector graphics and animation.
Strictly, WPF belongs to the .NET framework family rather than to ASP.NET (which is for web applications), but the full form is the same either way. It was introduced with .NET Framework 3.0 together with WCF (Windows Communication Foundation) and WF (Windows Workflow Foundation), which explains the word 'Foundation'.
So the answer is option A; 'Framework', 'Programming Force' and 'File' are distractors.

Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements?
i) Just-In-Time compiler (JIT) is a part of Common Language Runtime (CLR).
ii) NET Framework is part of the .NET platform, a collection of technologies for building apps for Linux, macOS, Windows, iOS, Android.
iii) ASP.NET applications are compiled codes, written using the extensible and reusable components or objects present in .Net framework.
transcription.printedErrors: Statement ii begins 'NET Framework' without the leading dot ('.NET Framework').
transcription.changes: il → ii; NEI → NET; macOs → macOS; iOs → iOS; ASPINET → ASP.NET; option numerals 1/il/ill/ili → i/ii/iii

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
Check each statement:
- i) **True**. The CLR (Common Language Runtime) contains the **JIT compiler**, which converts MSIL/CIL code into native machine code at run time.
- ii) **True** as worded. Microsoft's documentation describes .NET Framework as part of the .NET platform, a collection of technologies for building apps for Linux, macOS, Windows, iOS, Android and more. (.NET Framework itself runs on Windows; the cross-platform part is .NET Core/.NET, but the statement describes the wider platform.)
- iii) **True**. ASP.NET pages are compiled, not interpreted, and are built from the extensible, reusable components and objects of the .NET framework.

transcription.text: Which of the following is NOT a key driver of e-business?

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
The forces that push organisations to adopt e-business include:
- **Commercial benefits**: lower costs, wider market reach, faster transactions.
- **Requirements of customers and suppliers**: trading partners expect online ordering, tracking and integration.
- **A skilled and committed workforce**: people who can use and support the technology make e-business possible.
A **supplementary workforce** (extra or temporary staff added to the regular workforce) is not a driver of e-business adoption. It has nothing to do with why a firm moves its processes online. So the answer is option D.
This item reflects a textbook list of e-business drivers; the exact list varies between textbooks, but D is clearly the odd one out.

transcription.text:
Which of the following are management information system resources?
Resources:
i) Hardware ii) Software iii) People iv) Data

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
An information system, including a management information system, is built from several kinds of resources:
- **Hardware**: computers, peripherals and other physical devices.
- **Software**: programs and procedures that process the data.
- **People**: end users and IS specialists who run and use the system.
- **Data**: the raw facts stored in databases and knowledge bases.
Standard textbook models (e.g. O'Brien's) also list **network** resources, but every item given here is an MIS resource. So all four (i, ii, iii and iv) are correct, which is option A. The other options leave out at least one essential resource.

transcription.text:
Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements?
i) Clipping process determines each element into the visible and invisible portion. The visible portion is selected. An invisible portion is discarded.
ii) Clipping can be applied through hardware as well as software.
iii) Point clipping, area clipping and text clipping are the types of clipping.
transcription.changes: truthfulmess → truthfulness; Al → An; i) → ii); cam → can; ini) → iii); elipping → clipping; option numerals 1/il/ill/ili → i/ii/iii

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
Check each statement:
- i) **True**. Clipping divides each element of a picture into the part inside the clipping window (visible), which is kept, and the part outside (invisible), which is discarded.
- ii) **True**. Clipping can be done in software (algorithms such as Cohen-Sutherland) or in hardware (dedicated clipping circuits in graphics processors).
- iii) **True**. Types of clipping include point clipping, line clipping, area (polygon) clipping, curve clipping and text clipping.
All three are true, so the answer is option B.

transcription.text: Solid modeling is based on ______, ______ and ______ geometric representation of physical object.
transcription.changes: Restored word order and the three blanks

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
**Solid modeling** represents an object as a closed volume, not just as edges (wireframe) or faces (surface model). Its defining property is that the representation is:
- **Complete**: it holds enough information to answer any geometric question, e.g. whether a point is inside the object, or its volume and mass.
- **Valid**: it describes a physically realisable solid (no dangling edges or faces).
- **Unambiguous**: each representation corresponds to exactly one solid.
So the blanks are complete, valid and unambiguous, option A.
Why not the others: 'incomplete', 'varying' and 'undefined' contradict the purpose of a solid model, which is an exact, informationally complete description.

transcription.text:
What is the expected output of the following Python code?
print("\nDictionary Iteration")
d = dict()
d['lmn'] = 123
d['abc'] = 345
for i in d :
    print("%s %d" %(i, d[i]))
transcription.printedErrors: Options 2-4 show a stray closing quote after 'Iteration' (Dictionary Iteration’).
transcription.changes: " nDictionary → "\nDictionary; dictO → dict(); d''Imn'] → d['lmn']; dl'abc'l → d['abc']; print(*%s → print("%s; Imn → lmn in options

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
Step by step:
- `print("\nDictionary Iteration")` prints a blank line (from `\n`) and then `Dictionary Iteration`.
- `d = dict()` creates an empty dictionary; then `d['lmn'] = 123` and `d['abc'] = 345` add two key-value pairs.
- `for i in d:` iterates over the **keys**. Since Python 3.7, dictionaries keep **insertion order**, so the keys come out as `lmn`, then `abc`.
- `"%s %d" % (i, d[i])` prints the key (string) followed by its value (integer).
Output:
`Dictionary Iteration`
`lmn 123`
`abc 345`
This is option A. B and C put the value before the key, and D pairs the keys with the wrong values.

transcription.text:
Find the rank of the given matrix.
[ 1 5 6 ]
[ 2 3 4 ]
[ −1 2 2 ]
transcription.changes: Rebuilt the matrix from the image; option 1 was empty → '2'

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
Matrix rows: (1, 5, 6), (2, 3, 4), (−1, 2, 2).
**Step 1: determinant.**
det = 1(3·2 − 4·2) − 5(2·2 − 4·(−1)) + 6(2·2 − 3·(−1))
= 1(6 − 8) − 5(4 + 4) + 6(4 + 3)
= −2 − 40 + 42 = 0
So the rank is less than 3.
**Step 2: find a non-zero 2×2 minor.** From the first two rows and columns: 1·3 − 5·2 = −7 ≠ 0.
So the rank is **2** (option A). (Check: R₃ = R₂ − R₁ gives (2−1, 3−5, 4−6) = (1, −2, −2) = −(−1, 2, 2), so the rows are dependent.)
Why not the others: a 3×3 matrix can never have rank greater than 3, so 6, 9 and 4 are impossible.

transcription.text: Which of the following input devices is used to detect orientation and angular velocity?

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
A **gyroscope** sensor measures **angular velocity** (rate of rotation about the x, y and z axes). Integrating this rotation tells the device how its **orientation** has changed. Phones, game controllers and VR headsets use it for motion control and screen rotation.
Why not the others:
- **Light pen**: a pointing device that selects or draws on a CRT screen.
- **Magnetometer**: measures the strength and direction of a magnetic field (used as a digital compass); it gives heading, not angular velocity.
- **Proximity sensor**: detects nearby objects, e.g. turning off a phone screen near the ear.
So the answer is option B.

transcription.text:
Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements?
i) A compiler translates the entire source code line by line.
ii) Computer architecture refers to those attributes of a system visible to a programmer.
iii) The Reduced Instruction Set Architecture (RISC) computer organisation reduces the cycles per instruction at the cost of the number of instructions per program to increase the CPU performance.
iv) All the arithmetic and logical processing is performed by the Arithmetic Logic Unit under the supervision of a control unit.
transcription.changes: lime → line; 1l) → iii); orgamisation → organisation; option numerals 1/li/ili → i/ii/iii

subject: Computer Science
concept: Compiler vs interpreter; architecture vs organisation; RISC
explanation:
Check each statement:
- i) **False**. A compiler translates the **entire program at once** into object code; translating line by line is what an **interpreter** does.
- ii) **True**. Computer architecture is the set of attributes visible to the programmer (instruction set, data types, addressing modes, I/O mechanisms); organisation is how they are implemented.
- iii) **True**. CPU time = instructions/program × cycles/instruction × time/cycle. RISC lowers cycles per instruction (simple, often single-cycle instructions) but needs more instructions per program.
- iv) **True**. The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations, while the control unit directs and supervises it.
So i-False, ii-True, iii-True, iv-True: option B.

transcription.text:
A stack is a liner data structure in which insertion and deletion of elements are done at only one end, which is known as the top of the stack. Stack is called a last-in, first-out (LIFO) structure because the last element which is added to the stack is the first element which is deleted from the stack.
Top → L
M
N
O
P
Bottom → Q
Read the above paragraph and answer the following.
Which of the following items will be at the top in the stack after removing three items?
transcription.figureDescription: A vertical stack of six boxes labelled, from Top to Bottom: L, M, N, O, P, Q.
transcription.changes: Filled in the stack contents from the figure; options were empty → O, L, P

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
In a stack, removal (pop) always happens at the **top**, following LIFO.
Stack from top to bottom: L, M, N, O, P, Q.
- Pop 1 removes **L** → top is M
- Pop 2 removes **M** → top is N
- Pop 3 removes **N** → top is **O**
After three removals the stack is O, P, Q with **O** on top, which is option A.
Why not the others: L is the original top (no removal); N is the third item removed, so it is no longer in the stack; P would be on top only after four removals.

transcription.text:
Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements?
i) The ‘communications’, ‘Schedules’ and ‘Task lists’ are key functionality aspects of project management software to guide you in your decision.
ii) A data warehouse is a relational database that is designed for query and analysis rather than transaction processing.
iii) Software integration option is one of the criteria for selecting project management software.
transcription.changes: truthfuluess → truthfulness; second and third 'i)' → ii), iii); mana gement → management; option numerals 1/il/ill → i/ii/iii

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
Check each statement:
- i) **True**. When choosing project management software, the key functions to compare are communication/collaboration tools, scheduling (Gantt charts, timelines) and task lists or task management.
- ii) **True**. This is the standard definition (used, for example, by Oracle): a data warehouse is a relational database designed for **query and analysis** (OLAP) rather than for transaction processing (OLTP). It holds historical data drawn from many sources.
- iii) **True**. Whether the tool integrates with other software (e-mail, calendars, accounting, version control) is a common selection criterion.
All three are true: option A.

transcription.text: Which of the following languages is referred to as a database language?

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
**SQL** (Structured Query Language) is the standard database language for relational databases. It includes:
- **DDL** (CREATE, ALTER, DROP) to define structures,
- **DML** (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) to work with data,
- **DCL** (GRANT, REVOKE) and **TCL** (COMMIT, ROLLBACK).
Why not the others:
- **VJ++** (Visual J++) was Microsoft's Java development tool.
- **HTML** is a markup language for web pages.
- **Python** is a general-purpose programming language; it can connect to databases through libraries but is not itself a database language.
So the answer is option A.

transcription.text: Which of the following devices works at the network layer of the ISO-OSI reference model?

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
A **router** works at the **network layer (Layer 3)**. It reads the logical (IP) address in each packet and forwards it between different networks using its routing table.
Why not the others:
- **Hub**: Layer 1 (physical); it repeats incoming signals out of all ports.
- **Repeater**: Layer 1; it regenerates a signal to extend cable length.
- **Amplifier**: boosts an analog signal, also at the physical level.
(For reference: switches and bridges work at Layer 2, data link; gateways can work up to Layer 7.) So the answer is option B.
